note: Peer classifications derived from actual Broadway League weekly reporting data (2019-2026). Median sellable = total capacity ÷ num performances, median across all reported weeks. Venues require 15+ reporting weeks unless noted as strategic proximity peers.

peer_type_definitions.size: Venues whose median per-show sellable capacity falls within ±10% of Bushnell's (2,450–2,994 seats). Core apples-to-apples comparison group.
peer_type_definitions.size_extended: Venues within ±15% of Bushnell (2,314–3,130 seats) but outside the ±10% core. Useful context benchmarks.
peer_type_definitions.proximity: Northeast and New England markets — audience overlap, booking competition, and regional touring circuit peers of Hartford.
peer_type_definitions.market: Nonprofit performing arts centers anchoring mid-sized metro markets (roughly 600K–2.5M population) with subscription-driven programming comparable to the Bushnell model.

venues.synopsis: A 2,691-seat Art Deco landmark on Hollywood Boulevard opened in 1930, operated by the Nederlander Organization. One of the highest-grossing Broadway touring venues in the country and a National Historic Landmark. The most-reported venue in the dataset — a reliable size benchmark.

The Temple Hoyne Buell Theatre (2,839 seats) opened in 1991 as part of the Denver Performing Arts Complex. Operated by Denver Center for the Performing Arts, a nonprofit with a subscription model comparable to the Bushnell. Second-most reported venue in the dataset.

A restored 1922 vaudeville palace (2,800 seats) at Playhouse Square in Cleveland, the nation's largest performing arts center outside New York City. Owned by the Playhouse Square Foundation with a strong subscription base. The Cleveland market (2M metro) is a close structural parallel to Hartford.

The Boston Opera House (2,600 seats) is a restored 1928 venue in Boston's Theater District, operated by Live Nation. The primary New England regional touring anchor — 90 minutes from Hartford and the Bushnell's closest major market competitor for shows and subscribers.

Procter & Gamble Hall (2,719 seats) is the flagship theater of the Aronoff Center for the Arts, designed by Cesar Pelli and opened in 1995. Owned by Cincinnati Arts Association, it anchors the city's Broadway series in a nonprofit model closely mirroring the Bushnell.

The Segerstrom Center in Costa Mesa (3,000 seats) is a premier Southern California arts complex opened in 1986. A nonprofit presenting Broadway tours alongside resident symphony and opera companies. At the top of the ±10% size range.

One of the oldest operating opera houses in the United States (2,987 seats), built in 1857 and home to the Broadway series presented by the Kimmel Cultural Institute. A major proximity peer — Philadelphia is roughly 3 hours from Hartford and serves a comparable regional audience base.

A Beaux Arts landmark on Hennepin Avenue (2,579 seats) opened in 1921 and restored in 1993. Owned by Hennepin Arts, a nonprofit dedicated to arts-inspired community development. Premiered Disney's The Lion King national tour and remains the primary Broadway venue for the Twin Cities market.

venues.theatre: Hobby Center For The Perf. Arts
venues.synopsis: The Hobby Center's Sarofim Hall (2,650 seats) opened in 2002 as a modern nonprofit venue in downtown Houston. The primary Broadway touring destination for Houston and the Gulf Coast region, presenting shows through Broadway Across America.

A 1928 Art Deco landmark (2,807 seats) in downtown Seattle operated by STG Presents. One of the Pacific Northwest's premier performing arts venues, consistently achieving strong capacity utilization across Broadway touring productions.
A landmark 1929 atmospheric theatre (4,678 seats) in midtown Atlanta. Too large to be a size peer but included as reference given frequent reporting. Not classified.

venues.theatre: Dr. Phillips Center for the Performing Arts: Walt Disney  Theater
venues.synopsis: The Dr. Phillips Center in Orlando opened in 2014 with the Walt Disney Theater seating 2,700. A nonprofit venue serving as Orlando's primary home for Broadway touring productions, with strong capacity performance reflecting a robust subscription market.

The George S. and Dolores Dore Eccles Theater (2,452 seats) opened in 2016 as Salt Lake City's premier performing arts venue. Achieves among the highest avg capacity utilization in the peer group, reflecting strong subscription demand in a mid-sized market comparable to Hartford.

DPAC (2,712 seats) opened in 2008 in Durham, NC, operated by Nederlander and the City of Durham. One of the top-grossing mid-size performing arts venues in the country, with high subscription penetration and strong capacity utilization in the Research Triangle market.

A Frank Lloyd Wright-designed venue (3,000 seats) at Arizona State University in Tempe, opened in 1964. Consistently achieves among the highest avg capacity utilization in the peer group, reflecting strong subscription demand in the Phoenix metro market.

venues.theatre: Straz Center for the Performing Arts
venues.synopsis: The Straz Center's David A. Straz Jr. Hall (2,610 seats) opened in 1987 in Tampa. One of the largest performing arts centers in the Southeast, presenting Broadway tours and supporting multiple resident arts organizations.

A restored 1914 venue (2,286 seats) in downtown Baltimore, operated by France-Merrick Performing Arts Center. Baltimore is approximately 4 hours from Hartford and sits within the same Northeast touring circuit — a meaningful proximity peer for scheduling and market analysis.

The Providence Performing Arts Center (3,100 seats) opened in 1928 and is the primary Broadway touring venue for Rhode Island. Just 90 minutes from Hartford, it is the Bushnell's most direct geographic competitor in New England — audiences and subscribers overlap significantly.

A restored 1927 atmospheric theater (2,708 seats) in New Orleans, reopened in 2013 after Hurricane Katrina damage. Operated by ASM Global, it serves as the primary Broadway touring destination for the Gulf South region in a mid-sized nonprofit-adjacent market.

The Des Moines Civic Center (2,735 seats) opened in 1979, operated by Des Moines Performing Arts. A nonprofit venue with a subscription-driven Broadway model in a mid-sized regional market (680K metro) closely comparable in scale and model to the Bushnell.

A restored 1926 venue (3,200 seats) in downtown Buffalo operated by Shea's Performing Arts Center. Slightly above the size peer range but included as a strong proximity peer — Buffalo is within the Northeast touring circuit and about 5 hours from Hartford.

Keller Auditorium (2,992 seats) is Portland's primary Broadway touring venue, managed by Portland'5 Centers for the Arts, a nonprofit organization. Achieves strong avg capacity utilization reflecting subscriber demand in the Pacific Northwest market.

Proctors Theatre (2,690 seats) in Schenectady is a nonprofit performing arts organization managing multiple regional venues across the Capital Region. The closest geographic peer to the Bushnell in the Northeast touring circuit (under 2 hours), serving an overlapping New England/Upstate NY audience.

A restored 1928 atmospheric theater in Memphis, operated by the Orpheum Theatre Group. A nonprofit anchor for the Memphis arts community (1.3M metro) in a subscription-driven model — useful market comparison for mid-sized Southern markets.
The San Diego Civic Theatre (2,972 seats) opened in 1965, presenting Broadway tours through Broadway San Diego. A key market in the Southern California touring circuit with consistent programming.

venues.theatre: Chapman Music Hall At Tulsa PAC
venues.synopsis: Chapman Music Hall (2,365 seats) at the Tulsa Performing Arts Center serves as the primary Broadway touring venue for Northeast Oklahoma (1.0M metro). A nonprofit city-managed venue with a subscription series — useful mid-sized market benchmark.

A restored 1928 Spanish Baroque movie palace (2,779 seats) in Columbus, operated by CAPA. The primary Broadway touring venue for Central Ohio, achieving strong avg capacity reflecting high subscription penetration. Columbus (2.1M metro) is a well-managed mid-market comp.

Oklahoma City Civic Center Music Hall (2,500 seats) presents Broadway touring productions in a mid-sized Southern Plains market (1.4M metro). A city-operated nonprofit venue with a subscription Broadway series comparable in structure to the Bushnell.

Centennial Hall (2,400 seats) at the University of Arizona in Tucson is the primary Broadway touring venue for the Tucson market. Strong reporting history makes it a useful benchmark despite sitting just below the ±10% size range.

venues.theatre: Bass Concert Hall @ U of TX at Austin
venues.synopsis: Bass Concert Hall (2,933 seats) at the University of Texas at Austin, operated by Texas Performing Arts. One of the most active Broadway touring venues in Texas in the fast-growing Austin market.

The KeyBank State Theatre (3,400 seats) is part of Cleveland's Playhouse Square complex. Total capacity is larger but per-show sellable seats fall within the ±10% size peer range. Useful alongside Connor Palace for Cleveland market benchmarking.

A restored 1922 venue (2,347 seats) in Rochester, NY operated by Rochester Broadway Theatre League. Rochester (1.1M metro) is a close structural comp for Hartford — nonprofit, subscription-driven, Upstate NY market. About 4.5 hours from Hartford.

venues.theatre: Kentucky Center For The Perf. Arts
venues.synopsis: The Kentucky Center (2,406 seats) in Louisville opened in 1983 as the city's primary performing arts venue. Operated by Kentucky Performing Arts, a nonprofit presenting organization with a subscription Broadway series in a comparable mid-sized market (1.4M metro).

The Municipal Auditorium Music Hall (2,400 seats) in Kansas City is the primary Broadway touring venue for the region. A city-operated venue in a mid-sized Midwest market (2.2M metro), providing useful benchmarking for subscription-based touring performance.

venues.theatre: San Jose Center For The Perf. Arts
venues.synopsis: The San Jose Center for the Performing Arts (2,677 seats) serves the Silicon Valley market through Broadway San Jose. A key venue in the Bay Area touring circuit providing West Coast mid-market benchmarking.

venues.theatre: First Interstate Center for the Arts
venues.synopsis: The First Interstate Center for the Arts (2,700 seats) in Spokane presents Broadway tours serving Eastern Washington and Northern Idaho. Per-show sellable capacity falls within the size peer range.

TPAC's Andrew Jackson Hall (2,472 seats) in Nashville is the primary Broadway touring venue for Middle Tennessee. A nonprofit state-operated venue in a rapidly growing market — useful benchmark despite Nashville's atypical growth trajectory versus Hartford.
TPAC's Andrew Jackson Hall (2,472 seats) in Nashville — see Tennessee Performing Arts Center entry. Both names appear in League reporting for the same venue.

The Queen Elizabeth Theatre (2,929 seats) in Vancouver is operated by Vancouver Civic Theatres as the city's primary Broadway touring destination. Strong avg capacity reflects the robust Vancouver performing arts market.
A restored 1922 venue (2,700 seats) operated by Michigan Opera Theatre, presenting both opera and Broadway touring productions. Median sellable capacity falls squarely within the ±10% peer range.

A restored 1928 atmospheric theater (2,922 seats) in Syracuse, NY. A regional New York State peer serving a market similar in size to Hartford (650K metro), nonprofit-managed, subscription-driven. One of the most directly comparable venues for the Bushnell's market positioning.

Chrysler Hall (2,500 seats) in Norfolk is the primary Broadway touring venue for Hampton Roads (1.8M metro). A city-operated venue in a mid-sized coastal market — useful market comparison for nonprofit regional touring performance.

The Southern Alberta Jubilee Auditorium (2,690 seats) in Calgary presents Broadway touring productions in the Canadian market. Per-show sellable falls within the ±15% extended range — provides cross-border touring context.

The Northern Alberta Jubilee Auditorium (2,678 seats) in Edmonton presents Broadway touring productions in the Canadian market. Per-show sellable falls within the ±15% extended range — provides cross-border touring context.
The Adrienne Arsht Center's Ziff Ballet Opera House (2,400 seats) is Miami's primary performing arts venue. At the lower edge of the ±15% extended range — useful Southeast regional benchmark.

The National Theatre (1,672 seats) in Washington DC is one of the oldest continuously operating theaters in the US. Smaller than the Bushnell but a key proximity peer — DC is approximately 4.5 hours from Hartford and shares the Northeast touring circuit.

The Forrest Theatre (1,800 seats) in Philadelphia presents Broadway touring productions. Smaller than the Bushnell but a proximity peer — Philadelphia is the major metro approximately 3 hours south of Hartford in the Northeast touring circuit.

The Emerson Colonial Theatre (1,700 seats) is a restored 1900 venue in Boston's Theater District. Smaller than the Opera House Boston and the Bushnell but a key proximity peer in the New England market — often receives touring productions on the same circuit as Hartford.

The Murat Centre (2,171 seats) in Indianapolis is a historic venue presenting Broadway touring productions. Per-show sellable falls within the size peer range. Indianapolis (2.1M metro) mid-market nonprofit comparison.

The Palace Theater (2,627 seats) in Waterbury, CT is a restored 1922 venue 30 minutes from Hartford. The closest geographic touring venue to the Bushnell — directly in the Connecticut market and a critical proximity peer for audience and subscription overlap analysis.

venues.theatre: Jacksonville Center for the Performing Arts: Moran Theatre
venues.synopsis: The Moran Theatre (2,930 seats) at the Jacksonville Center for the Performing Arts presents Broadway tours in Northeast Florida. Per-show sellable falls within the ±10% size range. Borderline weeks of reporting but included for size benchmarking.

venues.theatre: Hanover Theatre and Conservatory for the Performing Arts
venues.synopsis: The Hanover Theatre (2,339 seats) in Worcester, MA is approximately 1 hour from Hartford. A nonprofit venue in Central Massachusetts that shares the New England touring circuit with the Bushnell — a meaningful proximity peer for regional programming and audience analysis.

The Shubert Performing Arts Center (1,651 seats) in New Haven is 45 minutes from Hartford and within the same Connecticut market. Smaller than the Bushnell and primarily a tryout house, but the most direct same-state competition for touring productions and Connecticut audiences.

The Birmingham-Jefferson Concert Hall (2,956 seats) is part of the BJCC complex, presenting Broadway tours in the Deep South market. Per-show sellable capacity falls solidly within the ±10% size peer range.

venues.theatre: Broward Center For The Perf. Arts
venues.synopsis: The Broward Center's Au-Rene Theater (2,700 seats) opened in 1991 in Fort Lauderdale. A nonprofit presenting organization serving the South Florida market and among the most active Broadway touring venues in the Southeast.

A restored 1928 movie palace (2,800 seats) in downtown Pittsburgh operated by the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. Home to Broadway in Pittsburgh and performance venue for Pittsburgh Ballet Theatre, Pittsburgh Opera, and Pittsburgh CLO. A multipurpose nonprofit model very similar to the Bushnell.

venues.theatre: Steven Tanger Center for the Performing Arts
venues.synopsis: The Steven Tanger Center (3,000 seats) opened in 2021 in Greensboro, NC. A newer venue that has quickly established strong Broadway touring performance, providing a benchmark for newer performing arts centers in mid-sized markets.

A restored 1927 vaudeville palace (2,611 seats) in Omaha operated by Omaha Performing Arts, a nonprofit. Its subscription-driven Broadway series and mid-market positioning in Nebraska/Iowa (960K metro) closely parallel the Bushnell.
